sentences.text: The Grid Interface Relay defines the operational boundary between the offshore farm and the external transmission system.
Grid Interface Relay is known operationally as Wildmere.
The farm exports electrical power through the Offshore Substation, Main Transformer, and export cable to the designated grid connection point.
The Export Cable Monitor provides measurements that support assessment of the export path.
The Grid Interface Relay exchanges authorized operating signals with the transmission system at the agreed interface.
The Grid Dispatcher sets external dispatch requirements within the applicable connection agreement.
The Fleet Dispatch Console allocates requested farm output among available generating units.
Dispatch commands remain subject to equipment capability, protection settings, and approved operating limits.
The farm reports measured active power at the grid boundary for operational monitoring and settlement processes.
Reactive power capability is managed in accordance with the connection agreement and current equipment conditions.
Frequency response functions are enabled only when the relevant operating mode is authorized and available.
Protection coordination prevents a fault on the external system from causing unnecessary disconnection of healthy farm equipment.
Loss of communications does not remove local electrical protection or equipment interlocks.
A Grid Constraint may require reduced export, revised dispatch, or temporary disconnection.
SCADA Gateway provides relay status and interface measurements to the farm monitoring environment.
SCADA Gateway produces the Session Revocation Receipt when an authenticated control session is terminated.
Maintenance Planning Engine uses the Squall Window Bulletin when reviewing the timing of planned work.
Amber Quay coordinates operational notices and control-room decisions affecting the farm interface.
Kestrel Bay reports its approach and departure status in accordance with the approved marine coordination procedure.
The Substation Operator confirms that switching actions affecting the export path are within the authorized work scope.
The Control Engineer verifies that dispatch changes are reflected in the applicable control settings before implementation.
Interface alarms are prioritized according to their effect on safety, equipment protection, and continuity of export.
Planned tests are coordinated to avoid conflicting with dispatch obligations or active maintenance work.
A return to normal export follows confirmation that the interface is stable and all required protections are available.
The Grid Interface Relay maintains the farm's dispatch boundary while allowing local systems to manage turbine-level operation.
